# ISSUE-311 plan

Expose the installed Maven/Gradle runtime closure only inside the existing Linux harness-tools restore boundary. This phase produces PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md only.

## Dimensions and gates

Approved dimensions: small / known / sensitive; approved execution profile: sensitive. Budget: 16 hours including planning, implementation and validation. A bounded installed-layout resolver and fixtures should fit one cycle; arbitrary distribution support would not. Require an independent security/design review of the closure rules and adversarial coverage, then the human plan approval required by WORKUNIT.md, before implementation. Reviewers must verify these proposals against approved inputs; this document grants no authority or approval.

## What we know

- `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:43` (`restoreFlags`) binds /usr/bin and /usr/lib plus fixed compatibility paths, but neither /usr/share nor /etc/alternatives. Launchers pointing there cannot resolve their installed runtime with those mounts alone.
- `internal/sandbox/restore.go:21` defines RestoreRequest as coordinator input, not candidate configuration. `:45` checks capability without payload execution; `:239` strips argv for that check. Preserve the generic canary's independence from installed Maven/Gradle availability.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_helper.go:22` runs descriptor closure, filesystem/network/broker canaries and READY/GO acknowledgement before payload execution; `:110` supplies a fixed payload environment including generated public JVM trust. Preserve this protocol and resource limits (`restore_linux.go:23`).
- `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go:64,196,286,349` already cover launcher flags, real boundary isolation, cleanup and source special files. `restore_test.go:260` covers invalid inputs; `restore_protocol_test.go` covers the registry broker transport.
- `internal/sandbox/executor_test.go:89` tests ordinary ToolExecutor isolation. Its real-boundary tests require SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1; restore mount changes must never propagate into that executor.
- `Makefile` defines make fmt and make check (lint, race tests, changelog check). The compiled policy additionally requires go build ./..., go vet ./..., go tool staticcheck ./..., and go test ./....
- Proposed new files below are absent in this supplied snapshot (filesystem existence checks). Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails); developer must confirm absence at the approved base before creating them. If present there, treat them as modifications and reconcile before work.

## What we're assuming

- Installed launchers were read directly in this snapshot: Maven uses boot/plexus-classworlds-*.jar and bin/m2.conf; Gradle hardcodes lib/gradle-launcher-4.4.1.jar. Link inspection confirms /usr/bin/mvn -> /etc/alternatives/mvn (ultimately /usr/share/maven/bin/mvn), /usr/bin/gradle -> ../share/gradle/bin/gradle, and Java through /etc/alternatives/java to /usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin/java. Operator evidence confirms individual library links into /usr/share/java. Snapshot owners are mapped to nobody; that is fixture evidence only, never a relaxation of production root ownership.
- A fixed manifest for the reported system-installed layouts is sufficient. Cheapest check: compare the fixture manifest with operator-provided launcher/library topology during independent review. Do not support arbitrary package managers, home installations or repository wrappers.
- Host installation files are coordinator-trusted only after ownership, ancestor permissions, type and canonical-path checks. A pathname under /usr alone is insufficient evidence of trust.

## Open questions

- No launcher-manifest design question remains: the fixed manifest below selects all permitted additions. Unknown layouts fail with an unsupported-layout error; implementation does not wait for another host inspection or environment gate.
- Will Maven 3.9 / Gradle 4.4 run with Java 25 under the existing finite limits? Operator PR review checks this separately. JVM compatibility or memory failures do not justify increasing limits, broad mounts, or blocking implementation on an unavailable host. Record incompatibilities for maintainer disposition.
- Approved-base absence of new files cannot be proven without Git metadata in this snapshot. Confirm at implementation checkout before creating those files.

## Design and exact touchpoints

Modify `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go` (`restoreCommand`, `restoreFlags`) to prepare validated runtime inputs before spawning Bubblewrap and add only narrow read-only staged mounts/validated namespace aliases. Keep the platform-neutral request API, non-Linux failure path and check-only behavior unchanged. Existing control-directory ownership/lifetime remains responsible for staging cleanup; no new public runtime-path option.

Create, subject to approved-base absence verification:

- `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go`: unexported `resolveRestoreRuntime`, `stageRestoreRuntime`, runtime manifest/mount types and bounded safe traversal helpers. Use existing `internal/safefs` APIs for root-bound reads and exclusive atomic staged writes; no new filesystem framework.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux_test.go`: resolver/staging table fixtures, mount assertions and adversarial tests.
- `changes/unreleased/311.md`: concise user-facing description of narrow trusted installed-runtime support.

Modify `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go`: extend flags assertions and add actual fixture launches. Modify `internal/sandbox/executor_test.go` only to add an unconditional ordinary-executor mount-plan regression if existing coverage cannot assert absence of the added runtime paths. No adapter, registry policy, helper, broker, native Codex, OCI, protected-file or documentation expansion.

### Fixed runtime manifest (approval covers these rules)

Only additions listed here are authorized. Existing /usr/bin and /usr/lib read-only mounts remain unchanged; this task does not claim to reduce their existing visibility. Added /etc and /usr/share parents are empty namespace directories, never host directory binds.

| Role | Permitted input / destination | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maven launcher | /usr/share/maven/bin/mvn | One regular executable; /usr/bin/mvn may link directly here or via exactly /etc/alternatives/mvn. Recreate that alternatives alias individually. |
| Maven bootstrap | /usr/share/maven/boot/plexus-classworlds-*.jar | Exactly one immediate match; `*` is a nonempty ASCII alphanumeric/dot/underscore/hyphen version token, including `2.x`. |
| Maven libraries | /usr/share/maven/lib/*.jar | Immediate matching files only, at least one; no recursion, ext, jansi-native, logging or conf imports. |
| Maven classworlds | /usr/share/maven/bin/m2.conf | Generated fixed bytes below; never read or follow host bin/m2.conf -> /etc/maven/m2.conf. |
| Gradle launcher | /usr/share/gradle/bin/gradle | One regular executable; fixed /usr/bin/gradle alias. |
| Gradle bootstrap | /usr/share/gradle/lib/gradle-launcher-4.4.1.jar | Required exact file. Other hardcoded launcher versions are unsupported in this manifest. |
| Gradle libraries | /usr/share/gradle/lib/*.jar and /usr/share/gradle/lib/plugins/*.jar | Immediate matches only, both directories nonempty; deduplicate bootstrap. No init.d or other directory traversal. |
| Java executable | /usr/bin/java -> /etc/alternatives/java -> /usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin/java | Exact chain, executable target and selected JDK root; no alternatives directory import or other JDK version discovery. |

Library basenames must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*.jar` (ASCII, 255 bytes maximum); no slash, whitespace, control characters or hidden files. Ignore unmatched ordinary siblings; reject matching directories/special files. Enforce at most 512 entries scanned per enumerated directory (including ignored entries), 1024 selected unique files overall, 64 MiB per JAR, 512 MiB total copied bytes, 1 MiB per launcher, 1 MiB per textual metadata file, 16 MiB per public security data file, 4096 bytes per pathname, 32 components per path and 8 symlink hops per resolution. Bound generated entries/aliases to 2048 and total mounts to 2048. Fail on the first exceeded budget before payload execution; never truncate a classpath or raise budgets automatically. Sort directory entries and final destinations bytewise; deduplicate identical validated targets and reject conflicting destinations.

Each selected JAR may be regular in its selecting directory or link to another matching basename in that same directory or to an immediate `/usr/share/java/<matching-basename>.jar`. Further hops stay within immediate /usr/share/java matching JARs; no return to another tool root. No directory symlinks for enumeration roots. Resolve relative `..` only when the normalized destination is one of these exact typed edges (Debian ../../java links are supported); reject every intermediate hop outside the permitted roots, even if it later returns. Cross-root rules apply per edge, not just to final canonical targets. Validate regular terminal file type, ownership and permissions, not just suffix. Materialize validated bytes at selected classpath paths; no need to expose /usr/share/java at all. Recreate only launcher/Java namespace aliases whose canonicalization is required. Never import arbitrary links wholesale.

Generated Maven classworlds bytes, including final newline:

```text
main is org.apache.maven.cli.MavenCli from plexus.core

[plexus.core]
load ${maven.home}/lib/*.jar
```

This deliberately omits host maven.conf, logging and optional extension directives. Maven settings.xml, toolchains.xml, mavenrc, Gradle gradle.properties, init.gradle, init.gradle.kts, init.d, user configuration, private keys and host trust stores are NEVER imported, even if beside permitted inputs or linked from a matching name. Repository build configuration still runs inside the boundary and gains no mount-selection authority.

### Exact JDK public metadata exception

Inspection found JDK conf symlinks, lib/jvm.cfg, lib/security/blocked.certs and public_suffix_list.dat pointing outside /usr/lib. Support these exact destination/source pairs only (J is /usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64, E is /etc/java-25-openjdk):

- J/lib/jvm.cfg -> E/jvm-amd64.cfg; accept only the installed public VM selection lines `-server KNOWN`, `-client IGNORE`, `-zero KNOWN`, `-dcevm KNOWN` plus comments/blank lines. No external VM path entries.
- J/conf/security/java.security -> E/security/java.security: public JVM security policy, required. Preserve installed algorithm restrictions. Parse Java-properties logical lines/escapes before validation; reject active `include` directives and configured external provider arguments/paths. Permit only the built-in provider names observed here: SUN, SunRsaSign, SunEC, SunJSSE, SunJCE, SunJGSS, SunSASL, XMLDSig, SunPCSC, JdkLDAP, JdkSASL, SunPKCS11, without arguments. Unknown provider configurations fail unsupported rather than pulling extra files. No recursive configuration closure.
- J/lib/security/blocked.certs -> E/security/blocked.certs and J/lib/security/public_suffix_list.dat -> E/security/public_suffix_list.dat: required public certificate-denial/domain data, copied individually.
- J/conf/net.properties -> E/net.properties and J/conf/logging.properties -> E/logging.properties: optional exact public networking/logging defaults, if present. No follow-on files are discovered or imported from values. Missing optional files add no input; unsafe present files fail.
- J/conf/security/policy/unlimited/default_US_export.policy and default_local.policy: required regular public policy files already under /usr/lib; validate presence without adding external mounts. No limited-policy or arbitrary policy-directory import.

All E inputs must be terminal regular files at those exact paths; no additional symlinks under /etc. Stage public E files individually at their exact E destinations so the existing read-only JDK links resolve. Do not mount E or J/conf directories. Explicitly exclude nss.cfg, management/** (including jmxremote access/password), accessibility, sound, swing, JAXP config, JFR profiles, fonts and legal/docs symlink closures. They are not needed for the supported headless restore startup; unknown requirements fail unsupported rather than becoming grants. J/lib/security/cacerts -> /etc/ssl/certs/java/cacerts is not followed/imported: existing generated /restore-trust/ca.jks remains the TLS trust source through unchanged JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS. Do not import /etc/ssl, PKCS11 configuration, NSS databases, login configuration or private keystores. This allowlist authorizes public configuration bytes, not transitive authority to discover other files or sockets. Security-file include/provider rejection is tested independently of live JVM availability.

### Runtime authority and closure

1. Select only fixed trusted launchers /usr/bin/mvn or /usr/bin/gradle when the coordinator payload's executable is that launcher (or its independently resolved canonical equivalent). Generic payloads and check-only nil argv add no runtime mounts. Never discover executables through PATH, JAVA_HOME, MAVEN_HOME, GRADLE_HOME, cwd, wrappers, build files, repository manifests, host caches or user configuration. Do not execute launchers, package managers, ldd or build code on the host to discover dependencies.
2. Define code-owned layout manifests for /usr/share/maven and /usr/share/gradle: exact launcher/support files, fixed boot/lib and Gradle lib/plugins JAR enumeration rules. Resolve /usr/bin/java through the specific /etc/alternatives/java link to its validated /usr/lib JVM target. Add only necessary individual aliases; never mount /etc/alternatives itself. Keep existing /usr/lib visibility unchanged. No broad /usr/share, /etc, home, cache or installation-tree directory binds.
3. Enumerate only the supported manifest's library entries, recursively following symlinks with hop/count/byte/depth bounds and cycle detection. Permit a library cross-link into /usr/share/java only for an individually validated regular JAR required by that manifest, including further versioned JAR links, materialized at their selected classpath destinations. This is a narrow typed cross-root edge, not permission to follow any path under /usr/share. Recreate necessary aliases within the staged namespace so launcher canonicalization/classpaths still work. Reject dangling links, path traversal, unexpected external targets, special files, mount destination collisions and broad parent destinations.
4. Validate every path component and symlink hop, not only the final target. Production inputs and ancestors must have trusted system ownership and must not be group/world writable. Reject paths into source/repository, /cache, host temp, user homes, credentials, settings.xml, gradle.properties, init scripts, private keys or unrelated /etc configuration, including when reached through an otherwise allowed JAR name. Do not import installation conf directories. Only the exact public JDK metadata above and generated Maven classworlds file may be added; unknown configuration requirements fail closed. A JAR filename alone is not sufficient authority.
5. Pin traversal to trusted roots and copy validated regular files into a private control/runtime snapshot using safefs; preserve necessary read/execute modes without privilege bits. Build aliases only from validated edges, never copy uncontrolled symlinks into a mounted directory. Copy from the validated open handle, revalidate metadata/identity where required and fail on concurrent replacement or mutation; never validate then bind a mutable host pathname. Stage bounded directory contents before constructing a deterministic sorted mount list. Mount selected staged files/subtrees read-only at exact runtime destinations, with only empty parent directories as needed.
6. Complete validation/staging before Bubblewrap or payload launch. Missing executable/library, unsupported layout, unsafe input or exhausted traversal budget produces a bounded error naming runtime/category and remediation (install a supported system layout); do not echo contents, host credentials or repository-controlled diagnostic text. Failed preparation leaves no result and removes staging. Installed client absence must not fail generic restore preflight or ordinary execution.

Trusted installation metadata determines what runtime bytes enter the boundary. Repository pom.xml/build.gradle/settings.gradle and plugins remain untrusted executable build code: they execute only after existing canaries inside the same isolated restore boundary. They cannot enlarge the runtime closure or broker authority.

## Implementation sequence

1. Independent reviewer scrutinizes the fixed manifest, cross-root JAR edges, ownership checks, pinned snapshot strategy and proposed negative tests; resolve findings in these artifacts. Obtain exact-content human plan approval through the normal coordinator workflow before implementation.
2. Confirm base/new-file status; implement bounded resolver/stager with a package-private fixture filesystem seam. Production roots/manifests remain fixed; tests cannot expose a public configurable host-root feature. Add unconditional table-driven tests first, including concurrent replacement and credential exclusion.
3. Integrate runtime preparation in the Linux launcher using the existing private control directory, preserving argv literal handling and all existing flags. Extend flag and cleanup tests. Do not require both tools installed when requesting one; do not inspect either for nil/generic argv.
4. Add deterministic installed-layout boundary fixtures for both tools with chained /usr/share/java links and Java-alternatives topology. Use synthetic executable/runtime markers to prove dependency access and completion inside Bubblewrap, not an installed JVM/client. Keep test-only roots confined to package-private fixture wiring that calls the same production validator and mount renderer. Fixture ownership trust may be injected only privately; production trust policy stays fixed.
5. Add negative tests and ordinary-executor non-widening assertions; add the changelog fragment. Run focused and required checks. Prepare operator review checklist for installed clients without turning those checks into capability/startup gates.

## HANDOFF

- Entry points: `restore_linux.go:27,43` (launcher/flags), `restore.go:239,243` (check-only and launcher call; preserve API), `restore_helper.go:22,110` (protocol/environment; preserve unchanged). New private resolver/stager symbols are described above.
- Extend `restore_linux_test.go:32,48,64,196,286` fixtures/capability/flags/isolation/cleanup; preserve `restore_linux_test.go:96` helper startup and `restore_test.go:202,260,440` snapshot/input/capability coverage. Reuse broker fixtures in `restore_protocol_test.go:51` unchanged.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestoreRuntime' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestore' -count=1`; `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestToolExecutor.*Runtime' -count=1`; `SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1 go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestToolExecutorBoundary$' -count=1` on a namespace-capable Linux runner. Detailed mappings and mandatory commands are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Additional evidence: direct reads of /usr/share/maven/bin/mvn, /usr/share/gradle/bin/gradle, Maven bin/m2.conf and /etc/java-25-openjdk/security/java.security; ls/find of JDK conf/security and lib/security links establish the fixed manifest above. `rg` is unavailable; used grep/find instead. safefs/root.go:148,161,210 supplies no-follow regular opens, bounded reads and exclusive atomic writes; safefs/file_unix.go:23 supplies no-follow/nonblocking descriptor opens. Keep per-hop trusted-system traversal private in the new Linux resolver; do not change safefs public API.
- Checked assumptions: read active contract, compiled policy, project/architecture/conventions and /swarm-plan command; inspected actual mounts and helper environment/protocol; searched restoreCommand/restoreFlags/RestoreRequest/RestoreBoundary call sites and existing tests; checked proposed file absence in snapshot. No installed-client compatibility or test-pass claim is made by this planning phase.
- Reopen plan if support needs broader directories/configuration, repository-selected dependencies, changed broker/network/resource/helper behavior, adapter work, a public path-selection API, or a filesystem facility unavailable in safefs. Do not silently widen scope. Unavailable live hosts are review gaps, not implementation startup gates.
- **What this change breaks:** `restore_linux_test.go:64` directly asserts restoreFlags contents: extend while preserving isolation assertions. `restore_linux_test.go:80,313` directly calls restoreCommand: preserve signatures and missing-bwrap behavior. `restore.go:243` and `restore_other.go:11` depend on the common launcher signature: preserve unchanged. `restore_helper.go:110` depends on fixed executable paths/environment: recreate only validated aliases and preserve environment unchanged. `executor_test.go:89` and toolchain mount tests depend on ordinary isolation: preserve ordinary mounts unchanged, add a regression. Existing restore broker/protocol/helper/startup tests remain unchanged except fixture reuse. No docs/templates/adapter callers require updates; repository search found launcher symbols confined to restore files. Add only the required changelog fragment.

Java/usr/bin/java ->etc/alternatives/java ->usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin/java. Specify exact permitted launcher/publicclasspath metadata vs NEVER settings.xml/gradle.properties/init scripts, fixed boundedpatterns/limits and crossrootlink rules. Prefer generated fixed classworlds metadata if importing hostm2.conf would grantdynamic config; no broadetc/share binds. Inspect JDKconf symlink publicsecuritymetadata requirements within approvedscope; do not silently grant unknownconfig. Resolve concrete design, not new environment gate. # ISSUE-311 test plan

All tests below are implementation work after independent design review and human plan approval. Planning writes only this artifact and PLAN.md; no implementation checks have been run.

## Acceptance 1: deterministic installed-runtime launch and clear failures

Add `TestRestoreRuntimeLayouts` and `TestRestoreRuntimeBoundary` in the proposed runtime test file / existing Linux boundary tests:

- Separate Maven- and Gradle-shaped installations with fixed /usr/bin launcher links into /usr/share/maven and /usr/share/gradle; fixed boot/lib and Gradle plugin JAR sets; Java link through the single /etc/alternatives/java alias into /usr/lib.
- Maven library links into individual /usr/share/java JARs, including relative and absolute versioned chains. Gradle library/plugin dependencies likewise resolve through validated manifest edges. The synthetic launcher must consume each required dependency marker and execute the synthetic Java endpoint; write a completion marker only under /cache. Compare output with expected content. Do not use actual Maven/Gradle/Java installations for fixture acceptance.
- Assert deterministic sorted mount output, exact selected paths, staged source provenance and read-only modes. Unrelated sibling sentinel files in /usr/share/java, installation configuration and /etc/alternatives must remain absent.
- Missing launcher, missing Java target, dangling library, missing required boot/plugin files, unsupported installation roots and unsupported config requirements fail before launcher/payload execution. Assert a test payload-start sentinel is untouched, errors identify runtime/category/remediation, and staging/output are cleaned up.
- Nil argv capability checks and generic commands work with neither Maven nor Gradle installed; one runtime never requires the other. Same validated runtime plan is used for actual launch; no host execution for discovery.

Commands:

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestoreRuntime' -count=1
go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestoreLinuxFlags|TestRestoreLinuxBoundary|TestRestoreLinuxFailureCleanup' -count=1
```

Resolver/staging/flag tests run unconditionally on Linux without listeners, namespaces, network, or installed clients. Actual fixture boundary launches use the existing narrowly classified `requireRestoreCapability` skips for unavailable infrastructure. A capable Linux CI/review runner must execute those launches; arbitrary startup/payload failures must fail, never skip. Record skips explicitly.

## Fixed manifest coverage (Acceptance 1 and 2)

Extend TestRestoreRuntimeLayouts with exact golden destinations for the PLAN manifest, not merely substring assertions. Include Maven's /etc/alternatives/mvn hop, bin/m2.conf symlink to a hostile /etc/maven/m2.conf, boot/plexus-classworlds-2.x.jar, all immediate lib JARs, Gradle's exact gradle-launcher-4.4.1.jar and plugin JARs, and Java 25 alternatives/conf links. Assert generated m2.conf has exactly the approved bytes and no optional ext/logging directives; the hostile host m2.conf is never opened. Synthetic launchers consume staged dependencies and public metadata and write completion only in cache. Assert /usr/share/java is absent while materialized JAR classpaths work.

Add TestRestoreRuntimePublicMetadata: exact E/J pairs for java.security, jvm.cfg, blocked.certs, public_suffix_list.dat, optional net/logging and required unlimited policies; missing required vs absent optional semantics. Assert generated trust is unchanged and host cacerts, nss.cfg, management passwords/access, settings.xml, toolchains.xml, gradle.properties, init scripts and unrelated /etc siblings remain absent. Test active Java security includes (also escaped keys and continued lines), non-built-in providers/provider arguments, wrong exact metadata targets and extra symlink hops fail before payload start. Commented include examples remain accepted. No metadata contents appear in errors. Fixtures model public data shapes; no live Java is needed for these assertions.

Add TestRestoreRuntimeLimits with at-limit and limit-plus-one cases for every numeric budget in PLAN.md, directory scan counts including ignored names, suffix/name restrictions, ambiguous bootstrap matches, missing Gradle bootstrap, deterministic sorting/deduplication and conflicting destinations. Sparse/streaming fixtures avoid allocating closure-limit data unnecessarily. Test legal Debian relative ../../java edges, multi-hop versioned JARs, prohibited cross-tool edges and intermediate escape-and-return links. Matching directories/special files fail without blocking; unrelated ordinary siblings are ignored. No recursion into ext/plugins subdirectories beyond the single approved Gradle directory.

Public metadata and limit tests run in the unconditional focused suite:

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreRuntime' -count=1
```

## Acceptance 2: adversarial boundary preservation and required checks

Add table-driven `TestRestoreRuntimeRejectsUnsafeInputs`, `TestRestoreRuntimeSnapshot`, and `TestToolExecutorRejectsRestoreRuntimeWidening` (names proposed):

- Reject every forbidden root through direct paths, intermediate directory links, absolute/relative links and multi-hop chains: /etc, /root, /home, source/repository, host temp and host caches. Permit only the exact Java alternatives edge, not siblings. Reject prefix lookalikes, traversal, loops, excessive closure size/depth, destination collisions and unknown layouts.
- Reject FIFO/socket/device entries without blocking; reject writable/untrusted-owner files or ancestors, privileged modes and concurrent path replacement/mutation. Use deterministic synchronization/hooks rather than sleep races. After successful staging, replacing host inputs must not change staged bytes. Assert no post-validation mutable host path is bound.
- Reject credential/config/private-key targets even when disguised as JAR links; place synthetic settings.xml, gradle.properties, init-script, home and key sentinels beside permitted dependencies and verify they are neither staged nor visible. Ensure errors/logs contain no sentinel contents. Do not claim arbitrary secret-content detection; inclusion authority is the fixed trusted file manifest and provenance checks.
- Repository pom/build files, wrappers, local JAR links, altered PATH/JAVA_HOME/MAVEN_HOME/GRADLE_HOME and injected host options must never influence mount selection. No dependency graph execution/discovery on the host.
- Run fixture payloads that attempt source/runtime/alias/parent writes, cache-symlink writes outside cache, reads of host home/credentials/private key and inherited descriptor sentinel, direct IPv4/IPv6/metadata/host-loopback sockets, and unapproved registry CONNECT requests. Assert denial and unchanged host/source sentinels. Retain successful registry-only fixture artifact transfer through existing broker.
- Assert exact namespaces, dropped capabilities, cleared environment, descriptor policy, fixed helper, READY/GO canaries, generated public-only trust, resource flags, cancellation and failure cleanup remain intact. Preserve all adversarial tests; no widened skip classification.
- Unconditional ordinary-executor command/mount-plan comparison proves no added restore-runtime mounts or path-selection authority. Retain the real ToolExecutor isolation test on capable runners. Never share the new resolver with native/ordinary executors.

Commands:

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestoreRuntime|TestToolExecutor.*Runtime' -count=1
go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestRestore' -count=1
go test -race ./internal/sandbox -count=1
SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1 go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestToolExecutorBoundary$' -count=1
make fmt
make check
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
```

Run formatting and all required checks in the writable implementation checkout using approved caches; planning sandbox is read-only outside active artifacts. Inspect the diff after make fmt, including protected paths and existing adversarial tests. `make check` includes race tests and changelog validation. Add `changes/unreleased/311.md` and verify only the planned implementation paths changed. New test names must be reconciled with implementation so focused commands actually execute tests.

## Independent review and operator PR checklist

Before implementation, an independent reviewer checks the manifest, per-hop allow rules, root/ownership and concurrent-change handling, credential exclusion, snapshot cleanup and ordinary-executor separation; a human then approves the exact plan/test-plan through the approved gate. Self-review is not a substitute. Neither review artifact nor this plan can grant coordinator authority.

PR review checklist, outside automated startup/capability gating:

- [ ] On the dogfood host, record installed Maven 3.9, Gradle 4.4 and Java 25 executable/link topology and versions; compare to supported manifest, including external Maven JAR links.
- [ ] Launch each installed client inside the same restore boundary using only approved registry access and clean generated cache/home/trust. Record version/startup and small unauthenticated dependency-resolution results, or concrete JVM/version/resource incompatibilities for maintainer disposition. Never run candidate build code on the host.
- [ ] Confirm runtime mounts remain narrow/read-only and canaries/resource limits/broker restrictions remain enabled. Do not change adapters, grants, credentials or ordinary networking to obtain a pass.
- [ ] Record actual fixture-boundary runs, required-check results and infrastructure skips. Live client checks are operator review evidence, not prerequisites for generic restore startup or fixture acceptance.
